transcript.text: I observed that I have been taking a lot
of trades where the MACD was negative.
I've been taking those trades because in
recent weeks we've had some big curls.
We had this initial move, it pulls back
and then we have this big curl back up
and I've nailed some of those and I've
gotten nailed on some of them. Some of
them work out really well and some of
them I've gotten smoked on and I'm
having a bit of a hard time deciphering
which curls are going to go back to the
highs and which ones won't. But as I
looked through the trades that I did
poorly on, what I recognized was that
the curls that have been doing better
have been on one of the top two leading
gainers. That's again not perfect. There
are some instances that have been
exceptions of that, but that's been
pretty consistent. Trading past the 9:30
opening bell and halt levels. That's
been a problem. I've struggled on days
where we've had dispersed attention
where the leading gainer hasn't been
that clean and traders are kind of
jumping from stock to stock playing hot
potato looking for the second or third
most popular and it just hasn't worked
out as well for me. I've struggled when
I missed the whole front side of the
move and then I traded at the very top.
I tend to overcompensate and all of that
has resulted in me falling victim to
FOMO. But I have also noticed that I've
done really well on some inverted head
and shoulder patterns when the stock has
been one of the leading gainers.
